name: Florida Keys Challenge
included: Housing, catered meals and shuttles. No tent needed.
cabinsNote: Rentals: Burnham Guides (official outfitter), Mary, mary@burnhamguides.com, 305-240-0650.

overview.title: One basecamp, a different paddle every day
overview.text: New this year: everyone stays in cabins at Seacamp on Big Pine Key, at Newfound Harbor, and paddles out from there. Each day you choose an easy, mid or long route, from mangrove-lined Coupon Bight to open-water crossings in the Content Keys.
minis: Easy, mid and long choices each day

days.title: Arrive and settle in
days.body: Check in from 1 to 5 PM at Seacamp. Dinner is at 6 PM, followed by the trip overview and safety briefing.

days.label: Days 2 to 6
days.title: Paddler's choice
days.body: Breakfast at 7:30 AM and a packed lunch, then pick the route that fits your day: easy, mid or long. See the paddle choices below. Everyone returns to the same basecamp each night.

days.title: Breakfast and farewell
days.body: Breakfast at 9 AM, then head home.

choicesNote: Each day offers routes at different distances. Pick the one that matches your energy, the wind and the tide.

choices.name: Little Swash Keys and Tarpon Belly Key
Big Torch and Little Torch Keys
Content Keys and Sawyer Key
choices.note: Includes about 12 miles of open water.

camps.name: Seacamp Association, Big Pine Key
camps.note: Cabin housing at Newfound Harbor. Meals are included.

boat: Sit-in sea kayak, at least 15 feet, with a rudder or skeg and a spray skirt. You need solid kayaking, rescue, wet-exit and swimming skills.
water: Non-inflatable Coast Guard-approved PFD, worn on the water
Bow line, 8 to 10 ft, secured so it cannot come loose
Grab loops at bow and stern
First aid kit in a waterproof cover
Repair kit (duct tape, sealant, waterproof tape)
Rain gear and a fleece or light jacket
Dry change of clothes in a waterproof bag
Water for the day and snacks (lunch is provided)
Boat with rudder or skeg (rentals through Burnham Guides)
land: Something to read, music or earplugs
faq: Dinner at 6 PM and an evening program at 7 PM. Programs include authors, historians and environmental experts, and one night of live music.
No. Housing, meals and shuttles are included in the trip fee.
No. This trip is for experienced sea kayakers, with solid kayaking, rescue, wet-exit and swimming skills. Contact Janice if you are unsure.
Open to all skill levels. Paddlers under 18 must be with a parent or guardian, with no more than two children under 12 per adult. A signed waiver and emergency contact are required. No pets.
What are the rules on the water?
Wear a non-inflatable PFD at all times. People-powered boats only. Follow park rules, including the alcohol ban, and respect private property along the river.
All payments are non-refundable, including for weather and water levels. Paddle Florida strongly recommends buying trip cancellation insurance from an outside provider.
Yes. Final details are emailed 7 to 10 days before the trip.
